# slate 0.1.0 file formats

All files are TOML. Unknown keys are errors (E0103), never ignored. Paths are relative to the project root (the folder with slate.toml).

## Project: slate.toml

Marks the project root. Commands find it by walking up from the given path.

### `slate.toml`

Project settings. Its folder is the project root; every path in the project is relative to it.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | table: project.project | **required** | Name and entry scene. |
| `display` | table: project.display | — | Output size and background. |
| `iso` | table: project.iso | — | Isometric grid geometry. |
| `sim` | table: project.sim | — | Simulation rate and seed. |

### `[project]`

Project identity.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | Project name. |
| `engine` | string | — | slate version the project targets, e.g. "0.1". `check` warns (W0205) if the running slate differs. |
| `main_scene` | path | `"scenes/main.toml"` | Scene used when a command is given no scene. |

### `[display]`

The rendered frame. Screenshots and the web player use exactly this size.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | integer 1–4096 | `640` | Frame width in pixels. |
| `height` | integer 1–4096 | `480` | Frame height in pixels. |
| `background` | color | `"#1d2330"` | Color behind everything. |

### `[iso]`

Isometric projection. A cell's diamond is tile_width × tile_height pixels; one unit of height is z_height pixels.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tile_width` | integer 4–1024 | `64` | Diamond width in pixels. Usually 2 × tile_height. |
| `tile_height` | integer 2–512 | `32` | Diamond height in pixels. |
| `z_height` | integer 1–1024 | `32` | Pixels per unit of height (z, block height). |

### `[sim]`

The fixed-step simulation. A frame is one simulation step.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tick_rate` | integer 1–1000 | `60` | Steps per second. |
| `seed` | integer ≥ 0 | `1` | Seed for all randomness. Playtests and `--seed` can override it. |


## Scenes: scenes/*.toml

A scene has optional `[scene]`, `[camera]` and `[ground]` tables, then any number of `[[entity]]` and `[[connect]]` tables. Entities get ids 0, 1, 2, ... in file order (an entry with `cells` makes one entity per cell).

### `scene file`

A level: ground, entities and the connections between their signals.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | table: scene.scene | — | Scene metadata. |
| `camera` | table: scene.camera | — | What part of the world is on screen. |
| `ground` | table: scene.ground | — | A rectangle of floor cells; also the bounds movers stay inside. |
| `entity` | [[entity]] | — | Things in the world, one `[[entity]]` table each. |
| `connect` | [[connect]] | — | Signal wiring, one `[[connect]]` table each. |

### `[scene]`

Scene metadata.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | — | Display name. Default: the file name. |
| `doc` | string | — | What the scene is for. |
| `seed` | integer ≥ 0 | — | Overrides the project seed for this scene. |

### `[camera]`

The camera looks straight down the isometric axis; it only pans.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | [x, y] | — | Grid point [x, y] at the middle of the frame. Default: the middle of the ground. |
| `offset` | [x, y] | `[0, 0]` | Extra shift in screen pixels [right, down]. |

### `[ground]`

Floor cells from [0, 0] to [size_x - 1, size_y - 1], drawn as a checkerboard.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | [x, y] int | **required** | Number of cells [x, y]. |
| `color` | color | `"#6fa86a"` | Floor color. |
| `alt_color` | color | — | Color of every other cell. Default: `color`, slightly darker. |

### `entity`

A thing in the world. Starts from an optional prefab; keys here override it (component tables merge key by key).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | name | — | Unique name, needed to reference it from [[connect]], playtests and `inspect --entity`. |
| `prefab` | name | — | Prefab to start from: `wall` loads prefabs/wall.toml. |
| `pos` | [x, y, z?] | `[0, 0, 0]` | Grid position [x, y] or [x, y, z]. +x is down-right on screen, +y is down-left, z is up. |
| `cells` | [[x, y], ...] | — | Place one copy on each listed cell instead of `pos`. Cannot be used with `name`. |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | Disabled entities are not drawn, not solid, cannot be tapped and run no behaviors. |
| `solid` | bool | `false` | Nothing can move into its cell. |
| `tile` | table: tile | — | Flat diamond on the floor (marks, pressure plates). |
| `block` | table: block | — | Isometric box (walls, crates, buildings). |
| `sprite` | table: sprite | — | Upright shape standing on the cell (characters, items). |
| `mover` | table: mover | — | Moves one cell per direction input. |
| `patrol` | table: patrol | — | Walks a fixed path of cells. |
| `wander` | table: wander | — | Walks randomly (seeded). |
| `trigger` | table: trigger | — | Emits signals when actors step on or off its cell. |
| `props` | table | — | Free-form game data shown by `inspect` and checked by `[[expect]] props`. Nothing in data files changes props at runtime (Rust game code can). |
| `allow` | ["W....", ...] | — | Warning codes that are intended for this entity and should not be reported, e.g. `["W0201"]` for deliberately stacked solids. Errors cannot be allowed. |

### `[[connect]]`

When entity `from` emits `signal`, apply `action` to entity `to`. Every entity emits `tapped` when tapped.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | name | **required** | Name of the emitting entity. |
| `signal` | name | **required** | Signal name, e.g. `pressed`, `released`, `tapped`. |
| `to` | name | **required** | Name of the target entity. |
| `action` | enable \| disable \| toggle | **required** | enable, disable or toggle the target. |


## Prefabs: prefabs/<name>.toml

`prefab = "wall"` starts an entity from prefabs/wall.toml; keys on the entity override the prefab's, and component tables merge key by key (`block = { color = "#f00" }` keeps the prefab's height).

### `prefab file`

A reusable entity template: prefabs/<name>.toml. Same keys as an entity, minus name/prefab/pos/cells.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | — | What the prefab is. |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | Disabled entities are not drawn, not solid, cannot be tapped and run no behaviors. |
| `solid` | bool | `false` | Nothing can move into its cell. |
| `tile` | table: tile | — | Flat diamond on the floor (marks, pressure plates). |
| `block` | table: block | — | Isometric box (walls, crates, buildings). |
| `sprite` | table: sprite | — | Upright shape standing on the cell (characters, items). |
| `mover` | table: mover | — | Moves one cell per direction input. |
| `patrol` | table: patrol | — | Walks a fixed path of cells. |
| `wander` | table: wander | — | Walks randomly (seeded). |
| `trigger` | table: trigger | — | Emits signals when actors step on or off its cell. |
| `props` | table | — | Free-form game data shown by `inspect` and checked by `[[expect]] props`. Nothing in data files changes props at runtime (Rust game code can). |
| `allow` | ["W....", ...] | — | Warning codes that are intended for this entity and should not be reported, e.g. `["W0201"]` for deliberately stacked solids. Errors cannot be allowed. |


## Components

Tables an entity or prefab can carry. An empty table (`mover = {}`) adds the component with defaults.

### `tile`

A flat diamond drawn on the floor at the entity's cell, above the ground.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#c9b26b"` | Fill color. |

### `block`

An isometric box filling the entity's cell. Left and right faces are shaded automatically.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#9aa0a6"` | Top face color. |
| `height` | number 0–64 | `1.0` | Height in z units. |

### `sprite`

An upright shape whose bottom edge stands on the middle of the entity's cell.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | circle \| rect \| diamond | `"circle"` | circle (ellipse filling size), rect or diamond. |
| `color` | color | `"#ffffff"` | Fill color. |
| `size` | [x, y] | `[24, 32]` | Width and height in pixels. |
| `offset` | [x, y] | `[0, 0]` | Shift in pixels [right, down] from the standing point. |

### `mover`

Moves one cell per `up`/`down`/`left`/`right` input: up = -y, down = +y, left = -x, right = +x. Every enabled mover responds to the same input. A press or hold moves on its first frame if the mover is ready, then every `step_frames` while held. Input during the wait is not queued: a press is dropped (logged as `blocked`, reason `cooldown`); a hold moves as soon as the wait ends. A refused move also starts the wait, so a held direction retries every `step_frames`. Solids, other actors and the ground's edge also block, each logged as a `blocked` event with its reason.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step_frames` | integer 1–600 | `8` | Frames from one move to the next. `hold` for `step_frames × N` frames gives exactly N steps. |

### `patrol`

Walks `path` one cell at a time (x first, then y), starting from its `pos` toward `path[0]` (or `path[1]` if it starts on `path[0]`). The k-th step attempt happens in step k × step_frames − 1, so it is visible from frame k × step_frames. A blocked attempt is retried at the next attempt time.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | [[x, y], ...] | **required** | Cells to visit, in order. |
| `step_frames` | integer 1–6000 | `30` | Frames between step attempts. |
| `mode` | loop \| pingpong | `"loop"` | loop: back to the first cell; pingpong: walk the path backwards. |

### `wander`

Every `step_frames` (attempt k in step k × step_frames − 1, like patrol), draws one number from the world's seeded RNG: stay, or try one step up/down/left/right. Runs with the same seed repeat exactly.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step_frames` | integer 1–6000 | `45` | Frames between steps. |
| `area` | [[x, y], ...] | — | Two corner cells [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] to stay inside. Default: the whole ground. |

### `trigger`

Watches its own cell. Emits `on_enter` when the first actor (an entity with mover, patrol or wander) arrives and `on_exit` when the last one leaves.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on_enter` | name | `"pressed"` | Signal emitted when the cell becomes occupied. |
| `on_exit` | name | `"released"` | Signal emitted when the cell becomes empty. |
| `only` | name | — | Only this entity (by name) counts. Default: any actor. |


## Playtests: tests/*.toml

Scripted input and checks, run by `slate test`. Any playtest can also drive `run`, `shot` and `inspect` with `--input`.

### `playtest file`

Scripted input plus expectations, run by `slate test`. `run`, `shot` and `inspect` accept it as `--input`.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test` | table: playtest.test | — | Which scene, how long, which seed. |
| `input` | [[input]] | — | Scripted input, one `[[input]]` per event. |
| `expect` | [[expect]] | — | Checks on world state or the event log. |
| `shot` | [[shot]] | — | Screenshots compared with reference images. |

### `[test]`

Playtest settings.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | — | What the playtest checks. |
| `scene` | path | — | Scene to run. Default: the project's main_scene. |
| `frames` | integer ≥ 1 | `300` | Number of frames (steps) to run. |
| `seed` | integer ≥ 0 | — | Overrides the project and scene seed. |

### `[[input]]`

One input event. Use exactly one of `press`, `hold` or `tap`. Input at frame N is applied by step N (the step from frame N to N+1).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | integer ≥ 0 | **required** | Frame at which the input happens. |
| `press` | up \| down \| left \| right \| confirm \| cancel | — | Press and release an action within the frame. |
| `hold` | up \| down \| left \| right \| confirm \| cancel | — | Hold an action down for `for` frames. |
| `for` | integer ≥ 1 | `1` | With `hold`: number of frames to hold. |
| `tap` | [x, y] | — | Tap the screen at pixel [x, y]; hits the topmost enabled entity drawn there. |

### `[[expect]]`

A check at `frame`. Either entity state (`entity` with `pos`/`enabled`/`solid`/`props`) or the event log (`event`, filtered by `entity`, `other`, `signal`, `reason`, counted with `at_least`/`at_most`). Events are counted if they happened *before* `frame`: an event logged as `[N]` happened in step N and counts from `frame = N + 1`. `entity` matches the event's subject and `other` its other party (`slate explain events` lists both for every kind).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | integer ≥ 0 | — | When to check. Default: the last frame. |
| `entity` | name | — | Entity to check, by name. |
| `pos` | [x, y, z?] | — | Expected position. |
| `enabled` | bool | — | Expected enabled state. |
| `solid` | bool | — | Expected solid state. |
| `props` | table | — | Expected values of these props (others are ignored). |
| `event` | input \| tap \| tap_miss \| moved \| blocked \| trigger \| signal \| action \| error \| custom | — | Count events of this kind that happened before `frame`. |
| `other` | name | — | With `event`: only events whose other party is this entity (the blocker of `blocked`, the actor of `trigger`, the emitter of `action`). |
| `signal` | name | — | With `event`: only count events about this signal. |
| `reason` | solid \| actor \| edge \| area \| cooldown | — | With `event = "blocked"`: only count refusals for this reason (e.g. `solid`, not `cooldown`). |
| `at_least` | integer ≥ 0 | `1` | With `event`: minimum number of matching events (0 when only `at_most` is given). |
| `at_most` | integer ≥ 0 | — | With `event`: maximum number of matching events. `at_most = 0` asserts it never happened. |

### `[[shot]]`

Render a frame and compare it with a reference PNG. Create or refresh references with `slate test --update-refs`.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | integer ≥ 0 | — | Frame to render. Default: the last frame. |
| `reference` | path | **required** | Reference PNG, relative to the project root (e.g. tests/refs/smoke.png). |
| `max_diff_pixels` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Pixels allowed to differ. |


## Runtime rules

**Frames.** The simulation advances in fixed steps (`[sim] tick_rate` per second). Frame N is the state
after N steps. An `[[input]]` at frame N is applied by step N. `run --frames 300` takes 300 steps;
`shot --frame 300` and `inspect --frame 300` show the state after them. Everything is deterministic: same
files + input + seed = same state hash and same pixels, on every machine.

**Coordinates.** Cells are `[x, y]` integers; `[0, 0]` is the top corner of the ground. +x runs down-right
on screen, +y down-left, z is height. Direction inputs move movers: `up` = -y, `down` = +y,
`left` = -x, `right` = +x. Screen position of grid point (x, y, z), in pixels from the top-left:
`sx = ox + (x - y) × tile_width / 2`, `sy = oy + (x + y) × tile_height / 2 - z × z_height`, where (ox, oy) is
chosen so the camera `center` (default: the middle of the ground) lands in the middle of the frame. A sprite's
bottom edge sits at its cell's (sx, sy); `offset` shifts it. `slate inspect --json` shows each entity's
`screen` rectangle, which is the easiest way to place things.

**Step order.** Each step: input (taps resolve to the topmost enabled entity drawn under the point and
emit `tapped`), movers, patrols, wanderers, Rust game systems, triggers, then signal dispatch through
`[[connect]]` tables. A step that dispatches more than 1000 signals is cut off (E0301).

**Actors and blocking.** Entities with `mover`, `patrol` or `wander` are actors. A move is refused when
the target cell is outside the ground, holds an enabled `solid` entity, or holds another enabled actor.

**Enabled.** Disabled entities are not drawn, not solid, cannot be tapped, run no behaviors and do not
count for triggers. `[[connect]]` actions `enable`, `disable` and `toggle` change this. Enabling a solid
entity where an actor stands does not push the actor out.

**Input.** Every enabled `mover` responds to the same input. Only actors set off triggers.

**Signals.** Every entity emits `tapped` when tapped. A `trigger` emits `on_enter` (default `pressed`)
when its cell goes from empty to occupied by an enabled actor and `on_exit` (default `released`) when it
empties. Occupancy is re-checked every step, so enabling or disabling an actor that stands on the cell
counts too (the signal comes in the next step's trigger phase). A trigger that is already occupied at
frame 0 does **not** emit: start the connected door in the state you want (e.g. `enabled = false`).

**Events.** Every step logs what happened and what was refused, with a sentence and structured fields.
Read them with `slate inspect --events` or `slate run --events`; `slate explain events` prints this table.

Every event has `frame` (the step that produced it: `[N]` happened in step N, so it is part of the state from frame N + 1), `kind`, `entity` (the subject), `other` (if any) and `message`.

| kind | `entity` (subject) | `other` | extra fields | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | — | — | pressed | Actions that went down this step. |
| `tap` | the entity hit | — | x, y, signal | A tap hit the topmost enabled entity under the point; it emits `tapped`. |
| `tap_miss` | topmost disabled entity under the point, if any | — | x, y, under_disabled | A tap hit nothing enabled. |
| `moved` | the mover | — | cause, from, to | One cell of movement. `cause` is the direction, `patrol` or `wander`. |
| `blocked` | the mover | the blocker (for `solid` and `actor`) | cause, from, to, reason, frames_left | A move was refused. `reason`: solid, actor, edge, area or cooldown. |
| `trigger` | the trigger | the actor that entered or left | signal, by | The trigger's cell became occupied or empty; it emits `signal`. |
| `signal` | the emitter | — | signal, connections | A signal was dispatched to this many `[[connect]]` tables (0 = nothing listens). |
| `action` | the target | the emitter | signal, action, before, after | A connection enabled, disabled or toggled its target. |
| `error` | the emitter | — | code, signal | A runtime error, such as more than 1000 signals in one step (E0301). |
| `custom` | set by game code | set by game code | set by game code | Logged by Rust game code. |


**Drawing.** Ground first, then tiles, then blocks and sprites back to front by `x + y`, then height, then
part (block before sprite), then file order (later entities on top).
Blocks shade their left and right faces automatically. A sprite's bottom edge stands on its cell's center.
